{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

blocks.text:
**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

- **Keys.** Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain

Audit results:

1. **quickjs** — clean (index.global.js has no remote URLs; the asyncify files clean apart from the ffi.mjs bare import which the overlay shim fixes).
2. **pyodide.js** — contains `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v` (the default indexURL when loaded from CDN — a version-agnostic prefix `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v${version}/full/`). Since we load pyodide.js from the vendor dir with loadPyodide() inferring indexURL from script location... wait, does the DEFAULT indexURL kick in? pyodide.js computes its URL from `document.currentScript.src` — when loaded locally, indexURL = the vendor dir; the jsdelivr constant is only a FALLBACK when currentScript is unavailable. But AC1 is a TEXT grep — the constant must not ship. Fix: a lock `replacement` rewriting the jsdelivr default to `./` in the vendored copy. Need to see the exact expression first.
3. **sql-wasm.js** — only a GitHub issue link in a comment — not a cdn. `https://github.com/...` doesn't match AC1 markers (jsdelivr|unpkg|cdnjs|https://cdn.). Fine.
4. **webllm +esm** — self-contained (no static imports! good), huggingface.co URLs are model-weight registry entries = DATA (weights, explicitly allowed per ticket: "weights are DATA... MV3's remotely-hosted-code rule does not cover them"). huggingface.co is not a CDN marker and not code-loading — but wait, does the +esm bundle dynamically import anything at runtime? `import("...")` grep found none. Also `new URL(..., import.meta)`? The +esm format may reference import.meta.url for wasm loading — webllm loads model wasm libs from the MODEL REPO (huggingface, data-adjacent...). Actually web-llm's model libs (llm-cpp.wasm) load from the model's huggingface repo at runtime — that IS remotely-fetched code at runtime! Hmm. But: this is exactly how the WEB build works today and the ticket's position: weights are data; the model-library wasm is part of the model repo (per-model, runtime). The ticket's AC2 only requires "web-llm construct (module-level smoke)". The CWS reviewer flagged only the jsdelivr URLs. huggingface model-lib loads are analogous to weights (runtime downloads from the configured model source). I'll keep them and note in the PR that model-repo artifacts (weights + per-model wasm libs) stay runtime (data-plane), citing the ticket's weights-are-data distinction. Hmm — actually wait. Let me be careful: is the model-lib wasm "code"? Yes, strictly it's code fetched at runtime. But it's also how the web app works today, and the ticket explicitly scopes vendoring to "remotely-loaded ENGINE" code (the jsdelivr engine bundles), keeping model-plane artifacts runtime. The ticket table says web-llm vendored = "built ESM bundle (self-contained)". OK — aligned with the ticket.
5. **litert +esm** — has `from"/npm/@litertjs/wasm-utils@2.5.0/+esm"` — a jsdelivr SUB-IMPORT (absolute path). Must vendor wasm-utils@2.5.0/+esm too + rewrite the import to the local file. Also litert-esm.js contains `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/` — probably in a comment or the SRI note ("www.jsdelivr.com/using-sri-with-dynamic-files" — a comment link). Need to inspect and rewrite/strip. The comment mention isn't a functional URL but AC1 greps text — must go. Let me look at the context.
6. **transformers.min.js** — contains `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/onnxruntime-web` — that's the DEFAULT wasmPaths for ORT. Rewrite to `./` (relative to the vendored file) at fetch time + vendor the ort wasm files. Also check for `ort-wasm-` names to know which wasm files to fetch. And check static imports in transformers.min.js (self-contained bundle?).

Also pyodide-lock.json — grep found no https URLs? "-- pyodide/pyodide-lock.json:" printed nothing. Good.

**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

This file is the repo source text; the published page is
`site/privacy.html` — keep both in sync (AGENTS.md). The `<!-- sec:<key> -->`
markers are the mechanical section anchors the compliance tests pin
(gh-1630 AC6).

## English

<!-- sec:collect -->
### 1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the
following data is handled by the app **on your device**:

- **Chat and conversation content** you send through fa — your prompts,
  the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
- **Provider API keys** you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI
  provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
- **Page content the agent reads** when you ask it to act on a page
  (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive,
  history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
- **Local files you attach** or files the agent creates for you in its
  sandbox.
- The developer receives **none** of the above. There is no telemetry or
  analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app,
  optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2
  and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

<!-- sec:handle -->
### 2. How we handle data

- **On-device processing.** Prompts, tool results, and files are processed
  on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no
  servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
- **AI requests.** When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and
  context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers
  **you** configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process
  your data under their own privacy policies.
- **Analytics (app only).** Where the platform makes it available, the
  mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only
  (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase
  Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) —
  never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. **The browser
  extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.**
- **Website analytics.** The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics
  4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets
  no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from
  the page.

<!-- sec:storage -->
### 3. Data storage

- Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox
  files — is stored **locally on your device or in your browser**: the
  platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), `chrome.storage` and
  extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes
  and downloaded model caches.
- Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is
  no fa account and no fa cloud.
- On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights)
  are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

<!-- sec:sharing -->
### 4. Data sharing

- We do **not sell** your data, and we do not share it with third parties
  for marketing.
- The only third parties that receive your content are the **model
  providers you explicitly configure** (your requests go directly to their
  endpoints).
- **Native messaging.** When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI
  helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between
  themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer
  or any server.
- Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar,
  contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you
  invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

<!-- sec:retention -->
### 5. Retention & deletion

- Local data persists until **you** delete it: clear a chat/session inside
  the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall —
  uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
- Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser
  storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
- Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per
  Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

<!-- sec:security -->
### 6. Security

- **Keys.** Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain
  (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app
  sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
- **Redaction.** A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and
  token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they
  are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
- **Approvals.** Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages,
  sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from
  ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
- The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code **from inside the
  package** (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to
  what its features call.

<!-- sec:children -->
### 7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the
equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly
collect personal data from them.

<!-- sec:changes -->
### 8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

- **October 15, 2026** — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store
  mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code,
  native messaging, no telemetry).
- **July 29, 2026** — first published version.

<!-- sec:contact -->
### 9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at
[github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues).

**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

{"content":"# Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)

**Effective date: October 15, 2026**

This policy covers the **Fa** applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and
the **Fa browser extension** ("fa — browser agent") — built on the
open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are
designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and
content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

This file is the repo source text; the published page is
`site/privacy.html` — keep both in sync (AGENTS.md). The `<!-- sec:<key> -->`
markers are the mechanical section anchors the compliance tests pin
(gh-1630 AC6).

## English

<!-- sec:collect -->
### 1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the
following data is handled by the app **on your device**:

- **Chat and conversation content** you send through fa — your prompts,
  the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
- **Provider API keys** you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI
  provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
- **Page content the agent reads** when you ask it to act on a page
  (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive,
  history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
- **Local files you attach** or files the agent creates for you in its
  sandbox.
- The developer receives **none** of the above. There is no telemetry or
  analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app,
  optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2
  and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

<!-- sec:handle -->
### 2. How we handle data

- **On-device processing.** Prompts, tool results, and files are processed
  on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no
  servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
- **AI requests.** When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and
  context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers
  **you** configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process
  your data under their own privacy policies.
- **Analytics (app only).** Where the platform makes it available, the
  mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only
  (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase
  Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) —
  never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. **The browser
  extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.**
- **Website analytics.** The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics
  4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets
  no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from
  the page.

<!-- sec:storage -->
### 3. Data storage

- Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox
  files — is stored **locally on your device or in your browser**: the
  platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), `chrome.storage` and
  extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes
  and downloaded model caches.
- Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is
  no fa account and no fa cloud.
- On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights)
  are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

<!-- sec:sharing -->
### 4. Data sharing

- We do **not sell** your data, and we do not share it with third parties
  for marketing.
- The only third parties that receive your content are the **model
  providers you explicitly configure** (your requests go directly to their
  endpoints).
- **Native messaging.** When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI
  helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between
  themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer
  or any server.
- Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar,
  contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you
  invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

<!-- sec:retention -->
### 5. Retention & deletion

- Local data persists until **you** delete it: clear a chat/session inside
  the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall —
  uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
- Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser
  storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
- Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per
  Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

<!-- sec:security -->
### 6. Security

- **Keys.** Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain
  (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app
  sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
- **Redaction.** A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and
  token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they
  are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
- **Approvals.** Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages,
  sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from
  ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
- The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code **from inside the
  package** (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to
  what its features call.

<!-- sec:children -->
### 7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the
equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly
collect personal data from them.

<!-- sec:changes -->
### 8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

- **October 15, 2026** — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store
  mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code,
  native messaging, no telemetry).
- **July 29, 2026** — first published version.

<!-- sec:contact -->
### 9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at
[github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues).

blocks.text:
**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

  `run_script(language, code)` runs `python` (pyodide, WASM CPython)

  the chrome hops are the typed `OffscreenApi` facade plus one

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

**Effective date: October 15, 2026**

This policy covers the **Fa** applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and
the **Fa browser extension** ("fa — browser agent") — built on the
open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are
designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and
content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

This file is the repo source text; the published page is

## English

<!-- sec:collect -->
### 1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the
following data is handled by the app **on your device**:

- **Chat and conversation content** you send through fa — your prompts,
  the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
- **Provider API keys** you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI
  provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
- **Page content the agent reads** when you ask it to act on a page
  (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive,
  history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
- **Local files you attach** or files the agent creates for you in its
  sandbox.
- The developer receives **none** of the above. There is no telemetry or
  analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app,
  optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2
  and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

<!-- sec:handle -->
### 2. How we handle data

- **On-device processing.** Prompts, tool results, and files are processed
  on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no
  servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
- **AI requests.** When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and
  context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers
  **you** configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process
  your data under their own privacy policies.
- **Analytics (app only).** Where the platform makes it available, the
  mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only
  (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase
  Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) —
  never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. **The browser
  extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.**
- **Website analytics.** The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics
  4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets
  no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from
  the page.

<!-- sec:storage -->
### 3. Data storage

- Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox
  files — is stored **locally on your device or in your browser**: the
  platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), `chrome.storage` and
  extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes
  and downloaded model caches.
- Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is
  no fa account and no fa cloud.
- On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights)
  are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

<!-- sec:sharing -->
### 4. Data sharing

- We do **not sell** your data, and we do not share it with third parties
  for marketing.
- The only third parties that receive your content are the **model
  providers you explicitly configure** (your requests go directly to their
  endpoints).
- **Native messaging.** When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI
  helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between
  themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer
  or any server.
- Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar,
  contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you
  invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

<!-- sec:retention -->
### 5. Retention & deletion

- Local data persists until **you** delete it: clear a chat/session inside
  the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall —
  uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
- Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser
  storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
- Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per
  Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

<!-- sec:security -->
### 6. Security

- **Keys.** Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain
  (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app
  sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
- **Redaction.** A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and
  token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they
  are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
- **Approvals.** Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages,
  sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from
  ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
- The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code **from inside the
  package** (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to
  what its features call.

<!-- sec:children -->
### 7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the
equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly
collect personal data from them.

<!-- sec:changes -->
### 8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

- **October 15, 2026** — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store
  mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code,
  native messaging, no telemetry).
- **July 29, 2026** — first published version.

<!-- sec:contact -->
### 9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at
[github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues).

blocks.text:
**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

- **`run_script` — sandboxed interpreters, web-app parity.** The SW
  cannot spawn processes and extension CSP forbids remote scripts, so
  `run_script(language, code)` runs `python` (pyodide, WASM CPython)
  and `javascript` (quickjs-emscripten) inside the MV3 offscreen
  document (`offscreen.html` + `offscreen/interpreters.js`), with the
  runtimes **vendored into the bundle** (`vendor/interpreters/`,
  downloaded by `scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh` at build time — the
  same versions the web app sandbox loads from a CDN). The SW side is
  `browser_ext/dart/src/run_script_tool.dart` (pure Dart, VM-tested);
  the chrome hops are the typed `OffscreenApi` facade plus one
  `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` bridge in `chrome_api_js.dart`. The
  document is created lazily on first call (reason `WORKERS`) and
  the curated config tool, never raw storage) plus path validation —
  only exact `chrome.<ns>.<method>` paths, no events (`on*`), no

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

**clipboardWrite** — Lets the agent place task results on the clipboard
when the user asks ("copy the answer", "put the extracted table on my
clipboard").

**contentSettings** — On user request the agent inspects and adjusts
per-site content settings (e.g. enabling JavaScript or notifications for
a site the user is automating) so user-instructed workflows run
correctly.

**contextMenus** — Adds fa's right-click entries ("Ask fa about this
selection/page/link") so the user can invoke the agent in context. One
rules for a workflow (e.g. block trackers on a page being tested,
simulate offline, strip a header that breaks an automation the user
asked for). Rules are scoped to the user's task.

**downloads** — The agent saves and manages files when the user asks
("download all PDFs linked here", "save this generated report"). Also
used to export fa's own artifacts (chat exports, screenshots) at the
user's request.

**fontSettings** — Read-only inspection of font settings when the user
asks the agent to diagnose rendering/readability issues of a page. Not
used to change anything without an explicit user instruction.

**history** — On the user's instruction the agent searches and reads
browsing history ("find that article I read yesterday", "reopen the
tabs from this morning"). History is processed locally; it is only
transmitted when the user explicitly asks the agent to summarize or
share it with the user's own model provider.

**identity** — Supports optional sign-in flows the user initiates (e.g.
account-backed features) via Chrome's identity plumbing. fa itself
works fully keyless/local; no identity data is collected by the
developer.

**idle** — Lets the agent detect user idleness so long-running
(diagnosing failing calls, waiting for an XHR the flow depends on).
Used for inspection/coordination, not modification; no request data
leaves the device except inside user-instructed summaries to the user's
own provider.

**desktopCapture** — On explicit user request only: share/record the
screen or a window when the user asks the agent to look at something
outside the browser ("help me with this dialog in another app").
Requires Chrome's own picker consent every time.

**pageCapture** — Saves a page as MHTML when the user asks ("archive
this page", "save a snapshot before you change it"). Snapshots are
local files in the user's Downloads.

{"content":" Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)
← Fa — Flutter Agent Harness

Privacy Policy

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.
