{"content":"# Privacy Policy — Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)

**Effective date: October 15, 2026**

This policy covers the **Fa** applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and
the **Fa browser extension** ("fa — browser agent") — built on the
open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are
designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and
content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

This file is the repo source text; the published page is
`site/privacy.html` — keep both in sync (AGENTS.md). The `<!-- sec:<key> -->`
markers are the mechanical section anchors the compliance tests pin
(gh-1630 AC6).

## English

<!-- sec:collect -->
### 1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the
following data is handled by the app **on your device**:

- **Chat and conversation content** you send through fa — your prompts,
  the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
- **Provider API keys** you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI
  provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
- **Page content the agent reads** when you ask it to act on a page
  (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive,
  history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
- **Local files you attach** or files the agent creates for you in its
  sandbox.
- The developer receives **none** of the above. There is no telemetry or
  analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app,
  optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2
  and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

<!-- sec:handle -->
### 2. How we handle data

- **On-device processing.** Prompts, tool results, and files are processed
  on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no
  servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
- **AI requests.** When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and
  context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers
  **you** configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process
  your data under their own privacy policies.
- **Analytics (app only).** Where the platform makes it available, the
  mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only
  (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase
  Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) —
  never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. **The browser
  extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.**
- **Website analytics.** The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics
  4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets
  no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from
  the page.

<!-- sec:storage -->
### 3. Data storage

- Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox
  files — is stored **locally on your device or in your browser**: the
  platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), `chrome.storage` and
  extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes
  and downloaded model caches.
- Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is
  no fa account and no fa cloud.
- On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights)
  are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

<!-- sec:sharing -->
### 4. Data sharing

- We do **not sell** your data, and we do not share it with third parties
  for marketing.
- The only third parties that receive your content are the **model
  providers you explicitly configure** (your requests go directly to their
  endpoints).
- **Native messaging.** When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI
  helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between
  themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer
  or any server.
- Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar,
  contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you
  invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

<!-- sec:retention -->
### 5. Retention & deletion

- Local data persists until **you** delete it: clear a chat/session inside
  the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall —
  uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
- Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser
  storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
- Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per
  Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

<!-- sec:security -->
### 6. Security

- **Keys.** Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain
  (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app
  sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
- **Redaction.** A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and
  token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they
  are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
- **Approvals.** Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages,
  sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from
  ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
- The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code **from inside the
  package** (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to
  what its features call.

<!-- sec:children -->
### 7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the
equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly
collect personal data from them.

<!-- sec:changes -->
### 8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

- **October 15, 2026** — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store
  mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code,
  native messaging, no telemetry).
- **July 29, 2026** — first published version.

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at
[github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues).

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

Now it's clear — and it's a semantic question, not corruption:

- The on-disk file (6065527 bytes) is the RAW download = byte-identical to the audit copy. The lock's sha256 (ae2f68) is the hash AFTER applying the replacement (6065513).
- Run 2's log line "fetched + verified (6065513 bytes)" — it verified the TRANSFORMED bytes and then... wait, but on-disk is 6065527 (raw). In the missing-file branch I do `os.replace(tmp, out_path)` BEFORE... no wait, let me re-read my script:

```python
data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
data = verify(data)       # transforms + checks
os.replace(tmp, out_path) # ← writes the RAW tmp, not the transformed data!
```

THAT'S THE BUG: I verify the transformed bytes but write the RAW tmp file. The transformed `data` (post-replacement) is never written. So:
- on-disk = raw (6065527), whose hash ≠ lock → verify-only fails (correctly detecting the inconsistency).
- The repair path (files that existed with drifted bytes): `data = verify(data)` on the OLD raw bytes — verify applies replacements → hash matches lock (since old raw == audit raw) → writes transformed bytes to .tmp → os.replace. So "repaired" files ARE correctly transformed on disk. That's why 4 files got "repaired" into correctness (they were written raw by run 1's partial... no wait, run 1 wrote raws too before timing out).

So the invariant design intent: **the lock pins the SHIPPED (post-transform) bytes; the staged files must BE the transformed bytes.** Fix the script: in the download path, write the TRANSFORMED data (not the raw tmp):

```python
data = verify(data)
with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f: f.write(data)  # hmm — but tmp holds the raw download; overwrite tmp with transformed then replace
os.replace(tmp, out_path)
```

Also the repair path: currently it re-VERIFIES old bytes but never downloads (the print lies). Restructure cleanly:

For each file:
1. Load expected: if on-disk exists and sha256(disk) == want → skip (already transformed).
2. Else if verify_only → fail loud.
3. Else download raw → verify (transform + hash check) → write transformed bytes atomically.

This handles both missing and drifted uniformly. Rewrite the python part of the script.

Found it — a real script bug: the download path verifies the transformed bytes but writes the **raw** tmp file. The lock pins post-transform bytes, so staged files must carry the transformed content. Fixing the script:

for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def transform_and_verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            """Apply the lock-declared replacements, then pin the hash.

            The lock's sha256 covers the SHIPPED (post-transform) bytes —
            the replacements are how remote constants are stripped out of
            the vendored bundles, so the staged file must carry the
            transformed content, never the raw download.
            """
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            if sha256(open(out_path, "rb").read()) == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk does not hash to "
                     f"the pinned {want}. The staged vendor tree is stale "
                     "or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")

        # Full mode: fetch (or re-fetch) the raw asset, transform, verify,
        # and stage the TRANSFORMED bytes atomically.
        tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
        # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
        subprocess.run(
            ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
             "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
            check=True,
        )
        data = transform_and_verify(open(tmp, "rb").read())
        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(tmp, out_path)
        fetched += 1
        print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified ({len(data)} bytes)")

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

Now it's clear — and it's a semantic question, not corruption:

- The on-disk file (6065527 bytes) is the RAW download = byte-identical to the audit copy. The lock's sha256 (ae2f68) is the hash AFTER applying the replacement (6065513).

```python
data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
data = verify(data)       # transforms + checks
os.replace(tmp, out_path) # ← writes the RAW tmp, not the transformed data!
```

THAT'S THE BUG: I verify the transformed bytes but write the RAW tmp file. The transformed `data` (post-replacement) is never written. So:
- on-disk = raw (6065527), whose hash ≠ lock → verify-only fails (correctly detecting the inconsistency).
- The repair path (files that existed with drifted bytes): `data = verify(data)` on the OLD raw bytes — verify applies replacements → hash matches lock (since old raw == audit raw) → writes transformed bytes to .tmp → os.replace. So "repaired" files ARE correctly transformed on disk. That's why 4 files got "repaired" into correctness (they were written raw by run 1's partial... no wait, run 1 wrote raws too before timing out).

So the invariant design intent: **the lock pins the SHIPPED (post-transform) bytes; the staged files must BE the transformed bytes.** Fix the script: in the download path, write the TRANSFORMED data (not the raw tmp):

```python

with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f: f.write(data)  # hmm — but tmp holds the raw download; overwrite tmp with transformed then replace
os.replace(tmp, out_path)

1. Load expected: if on-disk exists and sha256(disk) == want → skip (already transformed).
2. Else if verify_only → fail loud.
3. Else download raw → verify (transform + hash check) → write transformed bytes atomically.

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

Now it's clear — and it's a semantic question, not corruption:

- The on-disk file (6065527 bytes) is the RAW download = byte-identical to the audit copy. The lock's sha256 (ae2f68) is the hash AFTER applying the replacement (6065513).

```python
data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
data = verify(data)       # transforms + checks
os.replace(tmp, out_path) # ← writes the RAW tmp, not the transformed data!
```

THAT'S THE BUG: I verify the transformed bytes but write the RAW tmp file. The transformed `data` (post-replacement) is never written. So:
- on-disk = raw (6065527), whose hash ≠ lock → verify-only fails (correctly detecting the inconsistency).
- The repair path (files that existed with drifted bytes): `data = verify(data)` on the OLD raw bytes — verify applies replacements → hash matches lock (since old raw == audit raw) → writes transformed bytes to .tmp → os.replace. So "repaired" files ARE correctly transformed on disk. That's why 4 files got "repaired" into correctness (they were written raw by run 1's partial... no wait, run 1 wrote raws too before timing out).

So the invariant design intent: **the lock pins the SHIPPED (post-transform) bytes; the staged files must BE the transformed bytes.** Fix the script: in the download path, write the TRANSFORMED data (not the raw tmp):

```python

with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f: f.write(data)  # hmm — but tmp holds the raw download; overwrite tmp with transformed then replace
os.replace(tmp, out_path)

1. Load expected: if on-disk exists and sha256(disk) == want → skip (already transformed).
2. Else if verify_only → fail loud.
3. Else download raw → verify (transform + hash check) → write transformed bytes atomically.

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

Now it's clear — and it's a semantic question, not corruption:

- The on-disk file (6065527 bytes) is the RAW download = byte-identical to the audit copy. The lock's sha256 (ae2f68) is the hash AFTER applying the replacement (6065513).
- Run 2's log line "fetched + verified (6065513 bytes)" — it verified the TRANSFORMED bytes and then... wait, but on-disk is 6065527 (raw). In the missing-file branch I do `os.replace(tmp, out_path)` BEFORE... no wait, let me re-read my script:

```python
data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
data = verify(data)       # transforms + checks
os.replace(tmp, out_path) # ← writes the RAW tmp, not the transformed data!
```

THAT'S THE BUG: I verify the transformed bytes but write the RAW tmp file. The transformed `data` (post-replacement) is never written. So:
- on-disk = raw (6065527), whose hash ≠ lock → verify-only fails (correctly detecting the inconsistency).
- The repair path (files that existed with drifted bytes): `data = verify(data)` on the OLD raw bytes — verify applies replacements → hash matches lock (since old raw == audit raw) → writes transformed bytes to .tmp → os.replace. So "repaired" files ARE correctly transformed on disk. That's why 4 files got "repaired" into correctness (they were written raw by run 1's partial... no wait, run 1 wrote raws too before timing out).

So the invariant design intent: **the lock pins the SHIPPED (post-transform) bytes; the staged files must BE the transformed bytes.** Fix the script: in the download path, write the TRANSFORMED data (not the raw tmp):

```python
data = verify(data)
with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f: f.write(data)  # hmm — but tmp holds the raw download; overwrite tmp with transformed then replace
os.replace(tmp, out_path)
```

Also the repair path: currently it re-VERIFIES old bytes but never downloads (the print lies). Restructure cleanly:

For each file:
1. Load expected: if on-disk exists and sha256(disk) == want → skip (already transformed).
2. Else if verify_only → fail loud.
3. Else download raw → verify (transform + hash check) → write transformed bytes atomically.

This handles both missing and drifted uniformly. Rewrite the python part of the script.

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1630 I2 — fetch + verify the vendored engine assets from the lock.
#
# Every remotely-loaded engine the extension package carries is pinned in
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json (URL + post-transform SHA-256). This script
# is the ONLY sanctioned way vendor assets enter the package:
#
#   fetch_vendor_assets.sh [--lock P] [--dest D] [--verify-only]
#
#   default        download missing assets from the lock, apply the
#                  declared per-file `replacements` (each must occur
#                  EXACTLY once — that is how remote constants are
#                  stripped out of vendored bundles), verify the SHA-256
#                  of the final bytes, fail loud on any mismatch;
#   --verify-only  no network: verify the checksums of already-fetched
#                  assets (CI cache mode, the E1 selftest);
#   --dest D       target dir (default browser_ext/vendor — gitignored;
#                  the PACKAGE carries the bytes, the repo the lock);
#   --lock P       lock path (default browser_ext/vendor.lock.json).
#
# Replaces scripts/vendor_interpreters.sh (same interpreters/ layout, now
# checksum-pinned and covering ALL engines, not just the offscreen pair).
# Exit codes: 0 verified/fetched; 1 lock/dest missing, checksum mismatch,
# replacement count drift, network failure — NEVER a silent ship without
# verified assets (gh-1630 E1).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

lock=browser_ext/vendor.lock.json
dest=browser_ext/vendor
verify_only=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lock) lock="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dest) dest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --verify-only) verify_only=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "fetch_vendor_assets: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets requires python3 (lock parsing + sha256)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$lock" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: vendor lock not found: $lock" >&2
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$lock" "$dest" "$verify_only" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

lock_path, dest, verify_only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1"
try:
    lock = json.load(open(lock_path, encoding="utf-8"))
except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot parse vendor lock {lock_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def fail(msg):
    print(f"FATAL: fetch_vendor_assets: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

fetched = verified = skipped = 0
for engine, entry in sorted(lock["engines"].items()):
    version = entry["version"]
    for file in entry["files"]:
        name, url, want = file["name"], file["url"], file["sha256"]
        out_path = os.path.join(dest, name)
        replacements = [
            (old.encode(), new.encode())
            for old, new in file.get("replacements", [])
        ]

        def verify(data: bytes) -> bytes:
            for old, new in replacements:
                count = data.count(old)
                if count != 1:
                    fail(f"{name}: replacement {old[:48]!r} occurs {count}x "
                         "(lock contract: exactly once) — lock/reality drift")
                data = data.replace(old, new)
            got = sha256(data)
            if got != want:
                fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 mismatch — lock pins {want}, "
                     f"fetched(+replacements) hashes to {got}. Refusing to "
                     "ship unverified vendor assets (gh-1630 E1).")
            return data

        if os.path.exists(out_path):
            data = open(out_path, "rb").read()
            got = sha256(data)
            if got == want:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            if verify_only:
                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        else:
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
            tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
            # for the flaky big-wasm legs.
            subprocess.run(
                ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "4", "--retry-delay", "3",
                 "--retry-all-errors", url, "-o", tmp],
                check=True,
            )
            data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
            data = verify(data)
            os.replace(tmp, out_path)
            fetched += 1
            print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
                  f"({len(data)} bytes)")
            continue
        # Existing file with drifted bytes and full mode: verify() above
        # only runs on the freshly downloaded payload; re-verify the
        # written result too.
        data = verify(data)
        with open(out_path + ".tmp", "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
        verified += 1

print(f"vendor: {len(lock['engines'])} engines — "
      f"{fetched} fetched, {verified} repaired, {skipped} already verified")
PY
echo "fetch_vendor_assets: OK ($lock → $dest)"
","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}
